Hear from experts representing higher education, small business development, and digital marketing as they discuss practical applications of AI, emerging opportunities, potential challenges, and what business leaders should be considering as AI continues to evolve. title: Health & Wellness Seminar - The Neuroscience of Leading Without Burning Out
description: In this 45-minute keynote + Q&A, participants will explore the neuroscience of leading under pressure and discover how the R.I.S.E. Leadership Method™ can transform reactive, stress-based leadership into regulated, values-aligned, emotionally intelligent leadership. Through storytelling grounded in neuroscience research, participants will learn the four pillars of R.I.S.E. (Regulate, Integrate, Support, Empower) and gain immediately actionable tools to expand nervous system capacity, reduce burnout, and create cultures of psychological safety. This presentation integrates trauma-informed principles with evidence-based neuroscience, offering leaders a defensible, repeatable framework for sustainable performance and organizational transformation. Presented by: Alejandra Negrete Alejandra Negrete is the founder and CEO of Alex & Co. Consulting LLC, a neuroscience-based human performance and leadership development consultancy. A certified neuroscience coach and health coach, Alejandra brings over a decade of expertise in trauma-informed leadership, organizational culture transformation, and the R.I.S.E. title: Farm City Breakfast
location: 4175 Nopone Rd Gainesville ,
description: Farm City Breakfast Wednesday November 18, 2026 7:30am North Hall Community Center This event highlights agribusiness is the Hall County area and is a partnership between the UGA/Hall County Extension, Georgia Farm Bureau and the Greater Hall Chamber of Commerce. This years special guest is Ag Commissioner Tyler Harper. Tyler J Harper is Georgia’s 17th Agriculture Commissioner, a 7th generation farmer, a small businessman, and a proud native of rural South Georgia. A lifelong resident of the Peach State, Harper is a champion for Georgia’s #1 industry, the farm families who fuel its success, and all of rural Georgia. He knows that for Georgia’s farmers and producers, agriculture is more than just a job or a hobby – it is our way of life. Harper grows peanuts, cotton, and timber and runs a small cow-calf operation on land that has been in his family for over 100 years in Irwin County, Georgia. title: Industry Appreciation Luncheon
description: Industry Appreciation Luncheon Wednesday, November 18 11:30 am – 1:00 pm Lanier Technical College | Ramsey Conference Center Featuring the 18th Annual Industry of the Year Awards recognizing Economic Impact, Corporate Responsibility and Workforce Excellence. Join us for the Greater Hall Chamber’s Annual Industry Appreciation Luncheon celebrating the companies and people who help drive Hall County’s thriving industrial community. Kevin Price , President of the Georgia Ports Authority , is the guest speaker at the luncheon and will give an update on the Gainesville Inland Port. Price brings more than 30 years’ operations experience to Georgia Ports, having previously served as President of Gateway Terminals in Savannah and Chief Operating Officer of Virginia International Terminals. Georgia Ports is the nation’s third-busiest gateway for containerized trade in Savannah, and the #1 busiest auto port complex in the nation. Together, these form one of the largest economic engines in the Southeastern United States. title: Arbor Day
description: The community’s Annual Arbor Day Celebration is Friday, February 19 at 10 a.m. at Elachee Nature Science Center . Open to the public, the event is coordinated by the Greater Hall Chamber of Commerce and sponsored by the Hall County Master Gardeners , Keep Hall Beautiful and Georgia Power . Festivities include student contest recognition and a joint City of Gainesville/Hall County proclamation with Tree City USA recognition. The Greater Hall Chamber of Commerce Beautification Committee and the Georgia Forestry Service will recognize winners of the 2027 Arbor Day Student Art and Essay Contest. Dozens of student art and essay entries were submitted with the topic “I Speak for the Trees.” For information on Arbor Day or other Greater Hall Chamber Community Development programs, including Agribusiness programs and Business & Residential Beautification Awards, contact Robin Halstead, Greater Hall Chamber of Commerce, 770-532-6206 x 100.
